title: SRE standards: SLOs, error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling, and runbooks
author: Ari Chen
body:
Overview

This page defines Redwood Inference SRE standards for SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review expectations, operational tooling, and the canonical runbook templates used by oncall and platform teams. These standards apply to all production-facing services (hosted API, control plane, Dedicated controllers, and Private deployment control plane).

Scope & ownership

- Scope: production services, critical background workers, and control-plane components.
- Service owner: Product/Engineering team that owns feature/endpoint.
- SRE owner: SRE team assigned as reliability partner for the service.
- Oncall: primary and secondary SRE rotation.
- Review cadence: SLO review during quarterly reliability review or after major incidents.

SLO taxonomy and templates

Every service must publish an SLO document using the canonical template below (SLO document stored in service repo and referenced in Confluence). Use the following taxonomy:

1) Availability SLOs (error-rate based)
   - Tier 0 (critical control plane, auth): target 99.99% monthly availability (4.3m monthly error budget).
   - Tier 1 (core inference endpoints): target 99.95% monthly availability (~21.6m error budget).
   - Tier 2 (non-critical batch workers, analytics): target 99.0% monthly availability.

2) Latency SLOs (latency percentiles for successful requests)
   - P50 / P95 / P99 targets defined per endpoint; example for generation API: P95 < 300ms, P99 < 800ms for small models; for long-running model paths P95 < 1s.

3) Correctness/quality SLOs
   - For features where model quality is measurable (e.g., embeddings similarity, reranking accuracy) define a metric and target (e.g., mean reciprocal rank > 0.65 on canonical eval set).

SLO document template (required fields)

- service_name: short name
- owner: service owner (email)
- sre_partner: SRE oncall rotation team
- slo_targets: list of SLOs with metric, window (30d/90d), and target
- alerting_policy: link to alert definitions
- error_budget_policy: link to error budget runbook
- measurement: data source (Prometheus/SLO-exporter/BigQuery) and query
- burn_rate_thresholds: thresholds for automated mitigations

Error budget policy and procedures

Objective: keep feature development and reliability balanced. The error budget policy defines triggers and mitigation steps.

Key rules:
- Rolling 30-day window is the canonical budget window unless a different window is approved.
- Burn rate thresholds (default):
  - Normal: burn_rate < 1 (no action)
  - Watch: 1 <= burn_rate < 3 for 24+ hours -> SRE/PM notification and risk evaluation
  - Action: burn_rate >= 3 sustained for 6+ hours -> freeze risky launches, increase capacity, disable non-essential downstream jobs
  - Emergency: burn_rate >= 10 sustained 1h -> incident escalation to SEV/SEV+ process

Procedures:
1. If watch threshold exceeded: service owner + SRE review within 2 business hours; identify top contributing error classes; reduce load if possible (rate-limit, degrade features).
2. If action threshold exceeded: enact mitigation checklist (see runbook below), schedule rollback of recent changes, initiate short-term capacity increases if safe.
3. Document actions and update error budget page with timeline and residual budget.

Capacity planning (process and thresholds)

Goals: ensure headroom for 99.9th percentile demand spikes while minimizing cost.

Process:
- Monthly forecast: SRE + Platform run monthly capacity forecasts for GPU pools and control plane. Inputs: trailing 90-day qps, 95/99 usage percentiles, scheduled releases, expected sales-driven events.
- Headroom policy: target 25% headroom on GPU-backed inference pools for production routes; 40% headroom recommended during major launches.
- Burst policy: short-lived burst capacity via autoscaling for up to 15 minutes; sustained bursts >15m require capacity commit.
- Emergency capacity runbook: steps to increase node pool, failover region, or promote Dedicated capacity.

Operational thresholds and examples:
- Paging thresholds (example)
  - If 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes AND rolling error budget burn rate forecast > 1 -> page oncall.
  - If P99 latency > 3x target for 2 minutes on core generation route -> page oncall.
- Non-paging alerts
  - If queue depth > configured threshold or DB replication lag > 200ms -> notify owner with 1-hour SLA to acknowledge.

Reliability initiatives and program management

- Quarterly reliability objectives: each team proposes 1-3 initiatives tied to reducing errors, improving observability, or lowering cost-per-inference.
- Initiative lifecycle: propose -> estimate -> implement -> measure -> close. Each initiative must include owner, success criteria (metric delta), and target completion date.
- Example initiatives: KV cache improvements (reduce P99 latency by 20%), smarter batch-sizing (reduce GPU cost per token by 18%).

Incident review standards (blameless, timely, actionable)

Timeline:
1. Incident declared: within 24 hours owner posts initial timeline and impact summary.
2. Interim update: within 48 hours provide RCA hypothesis and mitigation steps.
3. Postmortem: completed within 7 calendar days for SEV≥2, within 14 days for SEV3.

Content required for postmortem:
- incident_id, severity, summary (one-liner), impact (customers, revenue, duration), detection method, timeline, root cause, contributing factors, mitigations (short-term and long-term), action owners, target dates, follow-up verification plan.
- Link to artifacts (traces, dashboards, logs queries).
- Blameless language: focus on systemic causes and process changes.

Incident review meeting cadence:
- Weekly incident review for SEV≥2 incidents until closure.
- Monthly reliability review meeting with SRE + service owners to track action completion.

Operational tooling (dashboards, alerts, runbook registry)

Canonical tooling:
- Metrics: Prometheus + Mimir for long-term; SLO-exporter writes SLO metrics into TSDB and BigQuery for historical analysis.
- Traces: Jaeger/Tempo with per-route sampling.
- Logs: structured JSON logs in Elastic/BigQuery with trace_id.
- Alerting: Alertmanager + Opsgenie; all paging alerts must include runbook link and troubleshooting checklist.
- Runbook registry: single source in Confluence (this page references service runbooks) and a link in PagerDuty/Opsgenie alert payload.

Recommended dashboards (example):
- Service overview: throughput, success rate, latency p50/p95/p99, error budget remaining.
- Capacity: node utilization, GPU memory pressure, queue depths, average tokens/sec.
- Cost: tokens served per GPU-hour, 95th percentile unit cost.

SRE runbook template and examples

All runbooks should be short, actionable, and tested during game days. Required sections:
- Title, service, severity level, pager (who to call), quick checklist, impact verification, mitigation steps (ordered), rollback steps, escalation path, post-incident notes.

Example: Core Generation API - high 5xx rate

Quick checklist:
1. Confirm alert: run PromQL: sum(rate(http_response_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) > 0.005
2. Identify recent deploys: git log --since='2 hours' --pretty=oneline origin/main
3. Check downstream dependencies: curl -sS https://internal-cache/_health || echo "cache-down"
4. If error class is model OOM: check GPU memory pressure dashboard and restart failing pods via kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-runtime
5. If traffic surge: apply rate-limiter: curl -X POST https://admin-api/services/<service>/config -d '{"rate_limit": 0.7}'

Escalation: if mitigations do not reduce error rate by 50% within 15 minutes, escalate to SEV lead and consider rollback.

Testing and game days

- Each critical runbook must be exercised at least twice per year via game days. Game days must include simulated detection and mitigation and a short game-day report.

Change control and rollouts

- Any change expected to impact SLOs must have a rollout plan documented and a canary phase (at least 1% of traffic for 30 minutes with SLO monitoring).

- Rollback criteria: if error budget burn rate forecast > 3 or latency P99 > 2x target in canary window -> automatic rollback.

Governance and review cadence

- Quarterly SLO review: SRE and service owners review SLOs, thresholds, and alert effectiveness.
- Annual compliance review for control-plane SLOs and incident processes with Security & Compliance.
